senses.gloss: m. (denom. of קַיִץ; v. קַיָּיט) attendant of summer fruits, watchman, fruit-picker &c.
units: <cite ref="Kiddushin 82b:4">Kidd. 82ᵇ</cite> <he>מימי</he> … <he>צבי ק׳ וכ׳</he> I have never seen a deer engaged in gathering fruits, a lion carrying loads &c.; Y. ib. IV, end, 66ᵈ <he>ארי ק׳</he> (corr. acc.); <cite ref="Tosefta Kiddushin 5:15">Tosef. ib. V, 15</cite> Var. ed. Zuck.—Pl. <he>קַיָּיצִים</he>, <he>קַיָּיצִין</he>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:6:3">Y. Ber. IV, end, 8ᶜ</cite> <he>ברועים ובק׳</he> in the case of shepherds and field-watchers (who are separated from communities assembling for prayer).

<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 24:15">Kel. XXIV, 15</cite> <he>של ק׳</he> leggings (or gloves) of fruit-pickers (v. <cite ref="Q02006"><he>פְּרַקְלִימִין</he></cite>); <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 2:11">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. II, 11</cite> <he>קיוצין</he> (corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 9:7">Mikv. IX, 7</cite> <he>מטפחת … של ק׳</he> the apron … of the fruit-pickers.—[
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 24:15">Kel. XXIV, 15</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 26:3">XXVI, 3</cite>; Mikv. l. c. (according to R. S.).]
